facts.statement: Keichousaurus is sometimes classified within Nothosauroidea but is more commonly listed as a separate, primitive lineage within Sauropterygia.
facts.quote: Keichousaurus, and the pachypleurosaur family broadly, are sometimes classified within Nothosauroidea, but are otherwise listed as a separate, more primitive lineage within Sauropterygia.

facts.statement: The holotype of K. hui was discovered in 1957 in Guizhou Province, China, and named by Young in 1958.
facts.quote: The holotype of K. hui, was discovered in the Falang Formation of Guizhou Province, China in 1957 by Hu Chengzhi and was named by Young (1958).

facts.statement: The species K. yuananensis was discovered in the Jialingjiang Formation of Hebei, China, and named by Young in 1965 based on a partial skeleton.
facts.quote: The second species, K. yuananensis, was discovered in the Jialingjiang Formation of Hebei, China and was named by Young (1965) based on the holotype specimen IVPP V.2799, a partial skeleton.

facts.statement: Most Keichousaurus specimens had small bodies, with sexually mature males reaching a snout-vent length of 12.6 cm and females 12.2 cm.
facts.quote: Most specimens had small body, males sexually mature with 12.6 cm snout-vent length (SVL), and in females by 12.2 cm SVL.

facts.statement: The mean snout-vent length for mature males is approximately 16.1 cm, while for mature females it is at most 14.9 cm.
facts.quote: Mean SVL for mature males is approximately 16.1 cm SVL, and for mature females, at most 14.9 cm SVL.

facts.statement: Keichousaurus is distinguished by its broad ulna, a feature that makes it unlike other European genera.
facts.quote: This fossil is distinguished by its broad ulna which makes it unlike other European genera.

facts.statement: Keichousaurus possessed a long serpentine neck, a relatively small head, and a long tail.
facts.quote: Keichousaurus also had a long serpentine neck with a relatively small head and long tail.

facts.statement: Keichousaurus lacked a sternum and had paddled-shaped forelimbs, suggesting the forelimbs were crucial for movement.
facts.quote: The sternum was also lacking in this animal, and the forelimbs were more paddled-shaped, possibly indicating a greater importance of the forelimbs in movement.

facts.statement: Keichousaurus likely used a rowing swimming motion powered by its paddle-like limbs.
facts.quote: Keichousaurus possibly utilized a rowing swimming motion using its paddle-like limbs.

facts.statement: Analysis of gut contents suggests Keichousaurus was a primarily piscivorous predator that used backwardly curved front teeth to catch prey and swallow it whole.
facts.quote: Based on analysis of exceptionally preserved specimens of Keichousaurus hui with preserved gut content, Keichousaurus is thought to have been a primarily piscivorous predator, catching prey with the backwardly curved teeth at the front of the mouth, and swallowing its prey whole.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that Keichousaurus young emerged from their mothers head first.
facts.quote: The young appear to have emerged from their mothers head first.

facts.statement: Keichousaurus lived during the Early to Late Triassic periods.
Keichousaurus is classified within the family Keichousauridae.
It is debated whether Keichousaurus and the pachypleurosaur family belong within Nothosauroidea or represent a separate, primitive lineage within Sauropterygia.
facts.quote: Keichousaurus, and the pachypleurosaur family broadly, are sometimes classified within Nothosauroidea, but are otherwise listed as a separate, more primitive lineage within Sauropterygia.
